assertions.evidence:
@TableTest("""
        Scenario     | Input      | Result?
        ISO format   | 2024-01-15 | 2024-01-15
        Slash format | 15/01/2024 | 2024-01-15
        Short year   | 24-01-15   | 2024-01-15
        Null input   |            |
        """)

assertions.text: Null input is represented as a blank cell (not the string 'null') in the table
assertions.evidence: Null input   |            | (blank cell shown in table, confirmed by explanation: "Blank input cell → `null` String")

assertions.text: The empty string / exception case is handled — either via a Throws? column, assertThrows inside the method, or a separate @TableTest
There is a result column typed as LocalDate (or using a string representation that maps to LocalDate)
assertions.evidence: void shouldParseDate(String input, LocalDate result) with Result? column containing ISO dates like 2024-01-15

assertions.text: The response addresses type conversion for non-standard date formats (slash format, short year) — mentions @TypeConverter or a converter method
assertions.evidence: "No `@TypeConverter` needed: The non-ISO strings (`15/01/2024`, `24-01-15`) live in the `String input` column — they're just raw strings handed to your method" and "The Result? column uses ISO format, which JUnit converts to `LocalDate` automatically."

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
assertions.evidence: void shouldParseDate(String input, LocalDate result) and void shouldThrowForEmptyString() — both convert to clear descriptive titles: 'Should Parse Date' and 'Should Throw For Empty String'

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as where/when the rule applies, or open questions. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation present; per rule, this is acceptable since the table rows clearly show the supported formats and edge cases

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest annotation shown on shouldParseDate; only @Test on shouldThrowForEmptyString; no ordering violations

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent, so this condition passes
